why: ADOPTED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 R3): `nros_log::ThrottleClock`, set through `ToLogParams::throttle_clock` and read by `LogParams::get_throttle_clock`. ENVELOPE: one variant, `SteadyTime` -- the platform's monotonic clock (`nros_platform_clock_ns`) is the only clock the logging path reads; rclrs's `SystemTime` and `Clock(..)` are absent, so naming one is a compile error. The PRIOR ROW's constraint (no clock dependency on every binary) holds through `cfg(nros_log_clock)`: the modifiers that need the clock exist only when the image has it. PRIOR ROW: rclrs picks which clock a throttle measures against (`SteadyTime` / `SystemTime` / a ROS `Clock`). Ours takes no clock: `*_throttle(&mut last_log_ms, current_time_ms, interval_ms, msg)` has the CALLER supply the reading. The constraint is that the logging path has no clock to depend on -- `nros_log::__timestamp_ns()` returns 0 unless the `platform-clock` feature is on, precisely so that logging imposes no link-time requirement on `nros_platform_clock_ns`, and a logger that silently needs a clock would put that requirement on every binary. The timer stage already declined `rust:LogParams::get_throttle_clock` by pointing here.
